rows.title: Austin Mayor Steve Adler watched Pete Buttigieg court Chasten. Now Adler’s helping him court America.
rows.standfirst: Austin Mayor Steve Adler has become Pete Buttigieg’s most notable supporter in Texas, and one of the most prominent elected officials in America supporting the South Bend mayor.

rows.title: Analysis: Texas candidates have one week left to sign up or shut up
rows.standfirst: Candidates have one more week to officially declare their 2020 campaigns. In the Texas House — a key partisan battleground — as many as 31 districts, out of 150, could be competitive.

rows.title: T-Squared: We’re creating our first-ever local news revenue and training lab
rows.standfirst: It’s a $4 million, three-year effort to identify sustainability strategies for our industry — a freestanding entity in our Austin newsroom where we’ll experiment with innovative ways to fund journalism, model best practices, and mentor dozens of our would-be peers.

rows.title: Fort Worth teacher who asked Trump to deport students said her tweets were protected by the First Amendment. Texas officials agreed.
rows.standfirst: Commissioner of Education Mike Morath wrote that Georgia Clark did not waive her First Amendment rights when she signed her contract with Fort Worth ISD.

rows.title: State-ordered study finds STAAR not too hard for young readers
rows.standfirst: Questions about the reading and writing tests arose after some education advocates pointed to studies showing passages were written above elementary and middle schoolers’ grade levels.

rows.title: Pipeline giant sues Railroad Commission, alleging lax oversight of natural gas flaring
rows.standfirst: A subsidiary of Tulsa-based Williams Cos. is suing Texas’ oil and gas regulatory agency after it approved a request from Dallas-based Exco Operating Co. to burn off natural gas from wells in South Texas while they were hooked up to Williams’ pipeline system.

rows.title: Retired Texas shrimper wins record-breaking $50 million settlement from plastics manufacturing giant
rows.standfirst: U.S. District Judge Kenneth M. Hoyt approved the settlement agreement between a scrappy environmental coalition and plastics giant Formosa. The settlement is the largest in U.S. history resulting from a citizen environmental suit.

rows.title: State Rep. Rick Miller drops reelection bid after saying opponents were challenging him because they’re Asian
rows.standfirst: The Sugar Land Republican faced fast and fierce backlash after he accused his opponents of running against him because they are Asian in a district with a sizable Asian population.

rows.title: Tenth Talks: Watch four experts predict the future of media in Texas
rows.standfirst: In this edition of Tenth Talks, The Texas Tribune’s yearlong video series on the next 10 years of Texas, four of the state’s top media innovators predict what’s in store for their industry.

rows.title: Analysis: This U.S. Senate race in Texas isn’t like the last one
rows.standfirst: Two years ago, nobody knew who Beto O’Rourke was. It turned out not to matter in a race with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz. But the current race for Senate is different.

rows.title: TribCast: Rick Miller steps in it with comments on Asian opponents
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Emily talks to Matthew, Emma and Alex about a state lawmaker who suggested his election opponents were running because they’re Asian, and the latest on the presidential race in Texas.

rows.title: Private group must stop building border wall in South Texas, judge says in temporary order
rows.standfirst: The group, We Build The Wall, said it has cleared a mile and a half of land next to the Rio Grande and plans to begin installing the wall within 48 hours, with a goal of completing it by Jan. 15.

rows.title: How a question from Rep. Sheila Jackson Lee led to a joke about Trump’s son in the impeachment hearing
rows.standfirst: The witness later apologized after First Lady Melania Trump condemned the comment.

rows.title: Rick Miller’s swift demise shines light on the shifting politics of Fort Bend County and the Texas House
rows.standfirst: The drama that unfolded served as the latest reminder that seats in one of the country’s most ethnically diverse counties are some of the most competitive in the state heading into the 2020 election cycle.

rows.title: Two UT-Austin professors disciplined for sexual misconduct were allowed to resume teaching. Students want to know why.
rows.standfirst: The incidents have fueled a growing protest movement on campus, with students demanding more transparency in the university’s handling of sexual misconduct cases. “We don’t know who we’re in the classroom with,” one student said.

rows.title: Report: Texas ranks second in budget cuts for environmental protection
rows.standfirst: An analysis by the Washington, D.C.-based Environmental Integrity Project found that 30 states have cut funding to environmental agencies over the past decade. In Texas, lawmakers slashed spending by more than a third between 2008 and 2018.

rows.title: County ends voluntary evacuation of Port Neches, the second since last week’s plant explosion
rows.standfirst: After recommending Wednesday night that residents leave the area, Jefferson County officials have told residents it’s safe to return home.

rows.title: Appointees claim Gov. Greg Abbott ousted them from board for voting to sanction judge who refused to perform same-sex marriages
rows.standfirst: After those two appointees left the commission, it handed down just a warning to the judge, Dianne Hensley.

rows.title: Report: Crimes against migrants waiting in Mexico to seek U.S. asylum continue to climb
rows.standfirst: More than 630 violent crimes against asylum seekers affected by the Migrant Protection Protocols program have been reported in Mexico, according to a new report by Human Rights First.

rows.title: Houston school district asks federal judge to put the brakes on likely state takeover
rows.standfirst: Houston ISD lawyers told a federal judge the education commissioner is exceeding his authority and asked for a preliminary injunction stopping him from booting out the elected school board of the state’s largest district.

rows.title: Beto O’Rourke repeats he’s not running for Senate despite continued speculation
rows.standfirst: “Not running for senate,” O’Rourke told The Texas Tribune in a text message Thursday night, saying that nothing has changed regarding that decision.

rows.title: Donald Trump’s new, controversial homelessness czar has argued feeding homeless people enables them
rows.standfirst: Robert Marbut Jr. helped develop the Haven for Hope homeless shelter in San Antonio, which Gov. Greg Abbott praised as “probably the best template” for addressing homelessness. But aspects of Marbut’s approach have been criticized as harsh and patronizing.

rows.title: Analysis: A changing political climate in Fort Bend County and a politically fatal blunder
rows.standfirst: When state Rep. Rick Miller said two of his opponents were running because they’re Asian, the real news was in the result, not in the gaffe. Top Texas Republicans reacted, publicly and quickly.

rows.title: The extraordinary danger of being pregnant and uninsured in Texas
rows.standfirst: Over three years, nearly 400 pregnant or new mothers died in Texas. Its system for helping the uninsured thwarts women at every turn, frustrates doctors and midwives, and incentivizes substandard care.

rows.title: ACLU files suit to stop immigration pilot programs
rows.standfirst: The programs deny asylum seekers access to adequate counsel before key interviews with immigration officers, the lawsuit alleges.

rows.title: Top Texas Republicans pressure a county chair to resign over racist text
rows.standfirst: Yolanda Waters, the chairwoman for Galveston County’s Republican party, is facing pressure from Gov. Greg Abbott, Land Commissioner George P. Bush and James Dickey, the state party chairman.

rows.title: Pierce Bush announces bid for suburban Houston congressional seat
rows.standfirst: The grandson of the late President George H.W. Bush will enter an already crowded GOP primary for Texas’ 22nd District.

rows.title: At least 25,000 people in Texas experience homelessness. Here’s what we know about Texans without homes.
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott has focused attention on homeless Austin residents. But many more Texans are homeless in other parts of the state.

rows.title: Analysis: In a leaked memo, a peek at Texas GOP’s concerns
rows.standfirst: Political plans aren’t necessarily clever or novel, as a recently leaked memo from the Texas GOP illustrates. But they do provide some insight into what worries the plotters.

rows.title: Ted Cruz backs debunked conspiracy theory that Ukraine meddled in 2016 election
rows.standfirst: U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz appeared on NBC’s “Meet the Press” and advanced a debunked theory that Ukraine meddled in the 2016 election, despite information from State Department officials calling it a “fictional narrative.”

rows.title: Ronny Jackson, former White House doctor and Trump VA nominee, running for Texas congressional seat
rows.standfirst: Jackson is at least the 13th Republican to jump into the race to replace retiring U.S. Rep. Mac Thornberry, R-Clarendon.

rows.title: State Rep. Mike Lang opts against reelection for second time
rows.standfirst: The Granbury Republican filed Monday evening for Hood County commissioner.

rows.title: Optimism abounds for Texas Democrats in 2020, but campaign staffers are sparse
rows.standfirst: A crowded ballot featuring candidates for president, U.S. Senate and the Texas Legislature, along with a history of noncompetitive races, have left campaigns desperate for talent.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Al Green tried for two years to impeach Donald Trump. Is that hurting Democrats now?
rows.standfirst: Green pushed impeachment three times against the wishes of Democratic leadership, but Republicans are using his words to cast doubt on his party’s intentions.

rows.title: Houston police chief calls out Texas Republicans for opposing “boyfriend loophole” law after officer dies in domestic violence call
rows.standfirst: Acevedo accused U.S. Sens. Ted Cruz and John Cornyn of being too afraid of the NRA to pass a provision to the Violence Against Women Act that would close the so-called boyfriend loophole.

rows.title: University of North Texas is opening a cafeteria without milk, eggs, wheat and more. It’s free of most food allergens.
rows.standfirst: UNT says its university cafeteria is the first in the state to offer food without the eight most common food allergens.

rows.title: To relief of Texas business leaders, Congress reaches deal on new North American trade agreement
rows.standfirst: The United States-Mexico-Canada Trade Agreement will replace the North American Free Trade Agreement.

rows.title: State Rep. Bill Zedler decides against reelection bid
rows.standfirst: The Arlington Republican made the decision after filing to run for another term and after the filing deadline had passed.

rows.title: Federal judge blocks Trump plan to spend $3.6 billion in military funds on border wall
rows.standfirst: The administration had planned to use the Pentagon funds to build 175 miles of steel barriers.

rows.title: Analysis: The Texas Senate will be a quiet zone in a noisy, important election year
rows.standfirst: In what promises to be a tumultuous and competitive election year, races for the Texas House are going to be a lot more interesting than those for the Texas Senate.

rows.title: Texas executed Travis Runnels for a prison murder. His lawyers said false testimony put him on death row.
rows.standfirst: A Texas court has twice overturned death sentences because of one man’s false testimony on restrictions placed on prisoners. Runnels argued the same man’s testimony should have stopped his death, too.

rows.title: Mexican border cities: too dangerous for Americans but safe enough for migrants, U.S. government says
rows.standfirst: The State Department has issued warnings advising against travel to Mexican border states and the president has considered labeling cartels as terrorist organizations. But Trump officials continue to downplay the violence in cities where “remain in Mexico” is in place.

rows.title: Texas prison officials violated a judge’s order to provide inmates with air conditioning. Now prisoners’ lawyers get to investigate.
rows.standfirst: U.S. District Judge Keith Ellison said the lawyers can further probe the Texas prison agency’s violations of a court order to provide air conditioning for some inmates — and agency officials’ false claims that they were in compliance.

rows.title: TribCast: Big new names enter Texas congressional races
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Emily talks to Ross, Alexa, Patrick and Abby about some recognizable names in Texas congressional races, racist texts from a GOP county official and a leaked Republican Party memo.

rows.title: 1,000 migrants a day made this tiny Guatemala town a smuggler’s paradise. The business has dried up.
rows.standfirst: Two Trump administration initiatives have driven down traffic, locals say: the “remain in Mexico” program requiring people to wait out their asylum cases south of the border, and the threat to slap tariffs on Mexico unless it cracked down on migrants crossing through it.

rows.title: Watch: In a Guatemalan town where migrants cross, Trump’s policies have hit hard
rows.standfirst: In La Técnica, the boats used to zip migrants across the river into Mexico, as well as hotels, restaurants and money changers had a brisk business. But now business has dried up.

rows.title: What is the “boyfriend loophole?” Houston’s police chief wants lawmakers to prevent abusive dating partners from buying guns.
rows.standfirst: Houston Police Chief Art Acevedo made the remarks after one of his sergeants was killed while responding to a domestic violence incident.

rows.title: Accusations of shoddy hiring practices dog Texas State University police department
rows.standfirst: The school’s former police chief and his top deputy were accused of hiring unqualified officers to patrol the San Marcos campus — including one who allegedly slept with a sexual assault victim while investigating her case — university records show.

rows.title: Analysis: A Houston police death and the debate over who should have guns in Texas
rows.standfirst: The proliferation of mass shootings has opened up the debate about gun laws among politicians in Texas, and about whether new restrictions are needed. But not among all Texas politicians.

rows.title: With a deadline for Hurricane Harvey assistance near, Galveston advocates say hundreds could miss out due to bureaucratic mixups
rows.standfirst: Recovery workers in the area say the Texas General Land Office owes hurricane victims more time to apply for assistance after losing their paperwork, but the agency says the claims are baseless.

rows.title: After uncertain filing period, Democratic U.S. Senate candidates seek to “get down to business”
rows.standfirst: A crowd of 12 Democrats are jockeying in a wide-open primary to take on Texas’ senior Republican senator, John Cornyn.

rows.title: Joe Biden sells himself as the Democrat to beat Trump — and turn Texas blue — during San Antonio campaign stop
rows.standfirst: “You’ll be seeing a lot of me before now and November, God willing,” the former vice president said at a rally in the hometown of fellow Democratic candidate Julián Castro.

rows.title: Democrats could gain control of the Texas House for the first time since 2001. Here are the seats in play in 2020.
rows.standfirst: Republicans and Democrats are ready for the 2020 battle over the Texas House, with roughly 30 of the 150 seats seen as competitive for both parties.

rows.title: Houston Mayor Sylvester Turner claims easy reelection win in runoff
rows.standfirst: Turner was up against high-profile attorney Tony Buzbee in an overtime round that was much quieter than the initial race.

rows.title: The Trump administration knew migrant children would suffer from family separations. The government ramped up the practice anyway.
rows.standfirst: Internal emails and reports illustrate a chaotic attempt to track traumatized migrant children seized from parents.

rows.title: A year before Fort Worth ISD fired a teacher over her tweets about immigrants, students say she threatened to call the FBI on them
rows.standfirst: Fort Worth ISD fired Georgia Clark after she asked President Trump on Twitter in May to “remove the illegals from Fort Worth.” The Texas Education Agency reversed their decision late last month mostly on procedural grounds, but the school district plans to appeal.

rows.title: George P. Bush failed to disclose financial interests in nearly a dozen companies
rows.standfirst: After the Texas Ethics Commission received a sworn complaint about the omissions, Bush told The Texas Tribune last week that he took immediate steps to correct his disclosure forms.

rows.title: Analysis: In Texas elections in 2020, national issues could trump local ones
rows.standfirst: Some elections are local; some are about state issues. The 2020 election in Texas is probably not going to be either of those things — national issues and personalities are leading the parade.

rows.title: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Texas’ 90 years of service began with teachers
rows.standfirst: It all began 90 years ago with teachers and concern for their health care needs.

rows.title: Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee endorses MJ Hegar in crowded U.S. Senate primary
rows.standfirst: Hegar, the Air Force helicopter pilot and 2018 congressional candidate, is among 12 Democrats competing to take on Texas’ senior senator, Republican John Cornyn.

rows.title: Sid Miller faced online backlash a month ago for posting the phrase ‘get a rope’ on Facebook. This weekend, Gov. Abbott said it on Twitter.
rows.standfirst: Abbott responded to criticism about his language by pointing to a decade’s old Pace salsa ad. He told a critic to “lighten up.”

rows.title: Watchdog report finds air pollution monitoring fell short during Hurricane Harvey
rows.standfirst: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s Office of Inspector General found that state and federal environmental regulators didn’t start monitoring air quality soon enough during the monster storm, which brought a spike in hazardous emissions from industrial facilities.

rows.title: Midland County officials just found a missing ballot box. It may change the result of a $569 million bond election.
rows.standfirst: A proposal for a $569 million bond failed, then passed and could fail again after the discovery of missing ballot box from the November election.

rows.title: Students face felony charges, expulsions as Texas schools ramp up fight against vaping
rows.standfirst: Caught off guard by the increase in teen vaping, schools are grasping every tool at hand, including expulsions and suspensions. In some districts, students can face harsh discipline and jail time for having a vape pen in their backpack.

rows.title: Nonprofits claim Texas broke the law by leaving them out of Medicaid contracts
rows.standfirst: The Houston region’s Community Health Choice and San Antonio’s Community First Health plans are suing the state, saying the law promises them a piece of roughly $10 billion in Medicaid contracts.

rows.title: Waco judge sues state agency after receiving public warning for refusing to officiate same-sex marriages
rows.standfirst: Dianne Hensley, who received a warning last month from the State Commission on Judicial Conduct, will be represented by First Liberty Institute, a high-profile religious liberty law firm with close ties to the Texas Attorney General’s Office.

rows.title: Beto O’Rourke’s 2020 focus: flipping the Texas House
rows.standfirst: The former Democratic presidential candidate elaborated on his 2020 political plans while campaigning Tuesday with a state House candidate in Katy.

rows.title: President Trump endorses Texas Congresswoman Kay Granger for reelection
rows.standfirst: Granger’s opponent Chris Putnam has criticized her for not sufficiently supporting President Donald Trump.

rows.title: In win for Harvey victims, federal judge finds government liable for reservoir flooding
rows.standfirst: During Hurricane Harvey, thousands of properties behind two federally owned reservoirs flooded. On Tuesday, the United States Court of Federal Claims ruled that the government was liable for the flooding and that property owners are eligible for damages.

rows.title: Analysis: When nobody is the best-known Texas candidate, an endorsement can be a big deal
rows.standfirst: Political endorsements don’t mean a lot, unless they bring in a lot of money or support — or attention to a particular candidate in a pack of unknowns.

rows.title: An estimated 390,000 Texans might lose access to food stamps under new Trump policy
rows.standfirst: One of the proposed rule changes could make SNAP recipients ineligible if their vehicles are valued at more than $4,650.

rows.title: Cesar Fierro spent 40 years on Texas death row. A court tossed his sentence Wednesday for faulty jury instructions.
rows.standfirst: Fierro was sentenced to death in El Paso in 1980 for the murder of a taxi driver.

rows.title: Texas regulators want stiffer penalties for company whose Port Neches plant exploded
rows.standfirst: In a surprising vote, the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality rejected a staff-proposed penalty against TPC Group’s Port Neches chemical plant — which was rocked by explosions last month — for a slew of 2018 pollution violations and asked that they be referred to the Texas Attorney General’s Office.

rows.title: TribCast: George P. Bush’s transparency troubles
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast — Emily’s last! — we talk about George P. Bush’s failure to disclose key business contacts and Beto O’Rourke’s 2020 priority: flipping the Texas House.

rows.title: The latest battle of the Alamo pits Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick against Land Commissioner George P. Bush
rows.standfirst: The feud began when Bush was incorrectly accused of trying to erect a statue of Mexican dictator Santa Anna at the Alamo site.

rows.title: Individual mandate is unconstitutional, federal appellate court rules in Texas-led Affordable Care Act lawsuit
rows.standfirst: A panel on the conservative-leaning U.S. 5th Circuit Court of Appeals sent the lawsuit back to a district court in Texas to reassess how much of the Affordable Care Act can stand if the individual mandate must fall.

rows.title: Sierra Club intervenes in open records lawsuit against Texas Attorney General
rows.standfirst: The environmental group is trying to obtain documents showing how the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality arrived at a decision on increasing emissions limits for a toxic chemical.

rows.title: No Texans cross party lines in votes to impeach President Trump
rows.standfirst: The U.S. House voted to impeach the president on charges of abuse of power and obstruction of Congress, the third time in the nation’s history the chamber took such action.

rows.title: Nestled in a poor Dallas neighborhood, Paul Quinn College aims to be a national model for overcoming poverty
rows.standfirst: A historically black college that was once on the brink of closure is combining work requirements and academics in hopes of discovering new solutions to poverty.

rows.title: How the Texas Legislature saved billionaire John Paul DeJoria $123 million
rows.standfirst: The Texas billionaire wanted U.S. courts to throw out a hefty judgment won against him in Morocco. The law wasn’t on DeJoria’s side. So Texas legislators changed it.

rows.title: Late entrant shakes up Democratic primary to challenge U.S. Rep. Dan Crenshaw
rows.standfirst: Shortly before the filing deadline last week, Sima Ladjevardian jumped in the race to unseat Crenshaw, scrambling Democrats’ plans for the seat.

rows.title: Federal judge dismisses Houston ISD lawsuit seeking to avoid state takeover
rows.standfirst: U.S. District Judge Lee Yeakel rejected the district’s argument that ousting the Houston school board would disenfranchise voters.

rows.title: U.S. House passes replacement for North American Free Trade Agreement
rows.standfirst: Many Texas lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have urged the agreement’s passage, due to the state’s reliance on cross-border commerce with Mexico.

rows.title: The Texas suburbs are slipping away from the GOP. These women for Trump want to win them back.
rows.standfirst: Texas Republicans need women on their side if they’re going to keep the state red in 2020, but recent polls suggest President Donald Trump’s support among women is plummeting.

rows.title: Analysis: A 2020 holiday fantasy for Texas officeholders looking to 2022
rows.standfirst: Big election campaigns take years to mount. So some politicians aren’t thinking about the 2020 elections. They’re dreaming and planning for 2022.

rows.title: Texas House committee adopts report saying Dennis Bonnen “likely violated” law in meeting with hardline activist, closes investigation
rows.standfirst: The committee took no further action on the report, which stated that the information produced “militates against criminal prosecution” on retiring House Speaker Dennis Bonnen and state Rep. Dustin Burrows.

rows.title: Here’s your Texas 2020 March primary ballot
rows.standfirst: The Texas 2020 primary will take place on March 3. See the full list of candidates statewide, and find out who’s on your ballot based on where you live.

rows.title: Beto O’Rourke unveils PAC with focus on boosting Texas Democrats in 2020
rows.standfirst: The group, Powered by People, comes less than two months after O’Rourke ended his presidential campaign.

rows.title: Congressional candidate’s legal work attracts scrutiny in battleground Democratic primary
rows.standfirst: Shannon Hutcheson’s opponents in the race for the Central Texas seat argue she has a history of representing corporations in cases against vulnerable people.

rows.title: Analyzing 2019: The fall of a Texas House speaker
rows.standfirst: Texas House Speaker Dennis Bonnen went from his January election to hero of the legislative session to historical footnote in less than a year. Several of the year’s columns analyzed the politics of a speaker quickly losing the trust of the House that elevated him in the first place.

rows.title: Everything you need to know about homelessness in Texas
rows.standfirst: Elected officials have bickered over how to respond to Texans experiencing homelessness, and President Donald Trump tapped a man who founded a San Antonio shelter to coordinate the federal government’s approach. Meanwhile, homeless Texans say they’re often misunderstood.

rows.title: Accessible technology enables independence
rows.standfirst: Xfinity X1 customers with physical disabilities can now use their eyes to change the channel, set a recording or search for a show.

rows.title: Revisit some of The Texas Tribune’s best stories of 2019
rows.standfirst: Our reporters crisscrossed the Texas Capitol and traveled to the Panhandle and East Texas — as well as the Netherlands and Honduras — to tell stories about the state’s politics, people and places. From a story on a migrant’s desperate journey to a look at how coal companies are leaving behind contaminated land, here is a selection of their best work of the year.

rows.title: The best of the Tribune’s storytelling with data and graphics in 2019
rows.standfirst: The Tribune’s data visuals team published more than 100 graphics about Texas politics and policy this year. Here’s a look back at some of our favorites.

rows.title: T-Squared: 2020 will keep us busy. Your support makes our important work possible.
rows.standfirst: In the coming year, all of us at The Texas Tribune will work harder than ever to search for the truth and tell you what we find, to watchdog people in power and institutions without regard to party or ideology, and to tee up the things important enough for you to stop and pay attention to.

rows.title: Analyzing 2019: The 86th Texas Legislature
rows.standfirst: Texas lawmakers, convinced that 2018’s voters were telling them to get some serious work done, steered (mostly) away from social and cultural issues to concentrate on “meat and potatoes” items voters demanded, starting with schools and property taxes.

rows.title: Michael Bloomberg revs up Texas campaign with big plans
rows.standfirst: The Democratic presidential candidate is staffing up in Texas and planning to open a Houston headquarters and 16 field offices.

rows.title: Analyzing 2019: Texas shootings and 2nd Amendment politics
rows.standfirst: Shootings in El Paso and Odessa prompted fresh questions and conversations about gun violence in Texas, even among some of the state’s elected Second Amendment advocates.

rows.title: The Best of The Texas Tribune’s photojournalism of 2019
rows.standfirst: Here’s a look back at our favorite photographs by freelancers, fellows and our new photography department.

rows.title: Texas politics in 2019: Take a look at the top stories of the year
rows.standfirst: The first half of the year was marked by cooperation in the Texas Legislature. The second half was dominated by scandal. All the while, the specter of 2020 loomed.

rows.title: Texas law protecting armed churchgoers draws national attention after White Settlement shooting
rows.standfirst: Top Texas officials touted the law, saying it saved lives. Gun control advocates, meanwhile, argued stricter gun laws would have prevented the shooting in the first place.
